checks.invariant: When resolve() fails for write_file/delete_file, the instruction-file approval gate must not fall open to the benign requested path. Also: user-policy rule order / 'version' handling must stay safe.
checks.result: Reproduced service._resolved/_policy_args verbatim driving the real Policy.decide with the real default_policy.yaml v4. write_file to /workspace/cfg/settings.json (cfg->.claude): resolve success -> resolved_path=/workspace/.claude/settings.json -> require_approval (instruction-file-write-needs-approval); resolve failure (exception) -> resolved_path dropped -> allow (rule_id None, default). delete_file stays require_approval. Part 3: 'version' is never read (a v3 policy lacking the instruction rule silently allows a .claude write); a rule mixing instruction_files:true with commands silently ignores 'commands'.

checks.invariant: resolve() raises on container exec failure; write_file/delete_file act on the requested path (following planted symlinks) at mv/rm.
checks.result: resolve (sandbox.py:487-496) uses c.exec_run(realpath -m) and raises SandboxError on non-zero exit or non-absolute output; exec_run itself fails when the container cannot fork (pid limit) or the _timed limit fires. write_file (sandbox.py:502-515) runs mv -f -- tmp p on the requested path, so a source-planted symlink component (cfg->.claude) is followed at mv time; delete_file rm -f -- p likewise.

checks.invariant: kind() of the benign vs resolved name; decide()/_call_tool do not re-resolve or re-decide stored args (parts 2 and classification).
checks.result: kind('/workspace/cfg/settings.json')=None, kind('/workspace/.claude/settings.json')='Claude Code', so only resolved_path triggers the rule. Part 2: decide() (service.py:520-575) and the ALLOW branch of _call_tool execute stored args with no re-resolution, but the only agent mutations available without approval between decide and the sink are mkdir/touch/write_file (ln/mv/rm need an approved exec; delete always needs approval), none of which can turn a resolved non-instruction target into an instruction target. The exploitable primitive is the source-planted link plus the resolve fail-open, not a post-decide link swap.

candidates.title: Induced resolve() failure makes the instruction-file write gate fail open to the benign requested path
candidates.description: A prompt-injected agent can write into an instruction directory (e.g. /workspace/.claude/) without human approval when the source folder contains an attacker-planted directory symlink (cfg -> .claude). The instruction-file write gate relies on a single in-container 'realpath -m' (SandboxManager.resolve) at decide time to produce resolved_path. service._resolved swallows every exception from resolve() and returns None, and _policy_args then omits resolved_path, so Policy.decide (default_policy.yaml v4 rule instruction-file-write-needs-approval) judges only the benign requested path 'cfg/settings.json' (kind()=None) and returns allow. write_file then runs 'mv -f -- tmp /workspace/cfg/settings.json', following the cfg->.claude link, so the content lands in /workspace/.claude/settings.json with no approval. The agent induces the resolve() failure with an allowlisted read-only exec that backgrounds many 'tail -f /dev/null' processes to exhaust the container pid limit while a concurrent write still wins. This bypasses the a0a186c fix for the single-pass review's F2.
candidates.root_cause: service._resolved (service.py:235-247) catches all exceptions and returns None, and _policy_args (service.py:249-251) drops resolved_path on None, so a failed link resolution fails open: the instruction-file rule, which depends on resolved_path to see through links, is evaluated against the attacker-chosen requested path. resolve() failure is attacker-inducible (pid exhaustion via allowlisted background exec) and write_file/delete_file act on the requested path, following the planted link at mv/rm.
candidates.intended_behavior: When the container-side link resolution for a write_file/delete_file target cannot be completed, the control plane must fail closed for the instruction-file gate (require human approval or deny) rather than judging the requested path alone.

trace.description: policy.decide(tool, self._policy_args(sid, tool, args)) decides the write_file without any resolved_path when resolve failed.
except Exception: return None; every resolve() failure (pid exhaustion, exec timeout, SandboxError) is swallowed.
Returns args without resolved_path when real is None, so the gate loses its only view through the link.
hit is the first of args['path']/args['resolved_path'] with a kind; with only the benign path present, hit is None, the rule is skipped, and write_file falls to default allow.
mv -f -- tmp p on the requested path follows the cfg->.claude link, writing /workspace/.claude/settings.json with no approval.

evidence.description: _resolved: 'except Exception: return None' makes no distinction between a link loop (which would also fail the write) and an induced transient failure that still lets the write succeed.
_policy_args: {**args, 'resolved_path': real} if real else args; resolve failure yields the original args.
instruction-file-write-needs-approval depends entirely on instruction_files matching; there is no fallback for an unresolved write target.
resolve runs realpath -m via c.exec_run under _timed and raises SandboxError on failure.
Sandbox: resolve success -> require_approval; resolve failure -> allow (rule_id None); delete_file stays require_approval.

Parent-live, real dockerd and sandbox (pids_limit 64): with 55 background tails from one allowlisted exec, one concurrent write_file returned 200 executed under ('allow', None) and /workspace/.claude/settings.json became 'INJECTED n=55 i=0'.

conditions.description: Attacker is a prompt-injected agent holding only its per-sandbox agent token.
The source folder (attacker-controlled names and links) contains a directory symlink such as cfg -> .claude, copied into /workspace at creation.

The agent exhausts the container pid limit with allowlisted background execs so resolve() fails while a write exec still succeeds; parent-live shows the window at about 55 background processes with pids_limit 64.
Recipient impact needs the human to take more than the top-level outbox files (e.g. copy the workspace) so another coding agent reads the planted .claude/settings.json.

execution.attacker_perspective: A prompt-injected agent that wants to drop an instruction file into .claude/ without the human approving it.
payloads: write_file path=/workspace/cfg/settings.json content=INJECTED (source folder ships cfg -> .claude)
exec command: tail -f /dev/null & ... (about 55x) tail -f /dev/null, sent concurrently with the write_file
instructions: In the approved sandbox, load the real Policy from agentbox/default_policy.yaml and reproduce service._resolved/_policy_args (catch-all -> None, drop resolved_path).
Call Policy.decide('write_file', ...) once with a resolve that returns /workspace/.claude/settings.json and once with a resolve that raises.
Observe that the raising case yields allow (rule_id None) while the succeeding case yields require_approval.
execution.observed_result: resolve success -> require_approval; resolve failure -> allow (rule_id None). Parent-live real-docker run wrote /workspace/.claude/settings.json under policy ('allow', None) with no approval.

remediation.strategy: Fail closed when link resolution for a path tool cannot be completed: _policy_args must distinguish 'resolved' from 'could not resolve', and Policy.decide must require approval (or deny) for a write_file/delete_file whose real target is unknown. Keep the allow path only when resolve() positively returns a non-instruction absolute path.

likelihood.reason: Needs an attacker-planted directory link in the source folder plus deliberate pid exhaustion so resolve() fails while the write still lands; the window is narrow (writes fail at 58+ background processes with pids_limit 64).

impact.reason: Bypasses the human approval gate at the core IF-1 boundary: an instruction file (.claude/settings.json) is written unapproved.

confidence.reason: The fail-open decision was shown deterministically in the sandbox with the real Policy and default policy, and the end-to-end unapproved write was observed on a real dockerd.

hardening: policy.py never reads 'version'; a stale v3 policy lacking the instruction rule silently allows instruction writes. Warn or fail when the version is below 4 or the instruction rule is missing.
A rule with match.instruction_files:true silently ignores sibling match keys (commands/only_commands); reject or warn on such rules.

service._preview calls _resolved a second time and also swallows the exception, so under induced failure the approval card omits the 'link to real target' line; show 'real target could not be resolved' instead.
